title: Make remote arcmux attribution continuously operational
description: Local Mission Control currently polls arcmux's mesh cache but has zero remote surface bindings, no populated current_work, and no durable recovery when an external peer transport dies. Deliver the persistent end-user outcome: real local cmux surfaces remain exactly attributed to their remote arcmux sessions and render live state plus semantic work context across peer disconnects and app/daemon restarts.
design: Use arcmux as the sole remote identity/session authority. Keep raw screen output owner-local; carry only allowlisted semantic summary metadata over authenticated mesh. Mission Control polls only local loopback projections and joins exact UUID/locator bindings. Treat transport supervision, current_work production, and surface binding as independent release gates.
acceptance_criteria: 1. At least one real devbox surface and one real labs surface are explicitly bound by stable local workspace/surface UUID to their exact remote device/profile/session locators. 2. Released Mission Control renders remote identity, state, freshness, and non-empty provenance-safe current_work for those surfaces. 3. New supervised agent surfaces receive authoritative arcmux bindings automatically; no title/cwd/recency inference. 4. Peer transport recovers after Wi-Fi/VPN/tunnel process loss without manual cleanup or rebinding. 5. Restart and disconnect dogfood proves same locators recover in the running released app on ref, with no private prompt/screen leakage. 6. Component issues remain open until the persistent live outcome passes, then tracker exports, releases, and cleanup complete.
notes: Parent goal created after correcting the earlier milestone-vs-outcome completion mistake. Related existing issues: mission-control-4f2 and arcmux-8lu; add the semantic current_work producer issue in arcmux.

title: Route Mission Control agent dispatch through arcmux supervision
description: Mission Control DispatchOutcome::NewSurface currently seeds raw claude/codex into a cmux terminal. Replace that path with an authoritative arcmux create + exact same-device cmux surface binding + supervised attach flow, using a single documented wrapper or protocol contract. Do not infer identity from cwd/title/session name. Until shipped, raw surfaces must be labeled not arcmux-supervised and remain ineligible for H handoff.
acceptance_criteria: 1. New Claude/Codex dispatches create an arcmux-supervised session. 2. The new cmux surface receives an exact same-device surface UUID binding to that arcmux locator. 3. The surface becomes H-eligible without title/cwd inference. 4. Every failure leaves the raw surface visibly unsupervised and reports an error. 5. Fake-command and live cmux/arcmux tests cover create, bind, attach, and rollback ordering.
notes: 2026-07-16 Mission Control implementation complete: exact cmux window/workspace/surface UUID resolution; strict arcmux create + owner catalog proof + local device/tmux identity + durable bind + attach + ready + goal send; bounded stdout/stderr/stdin and timeouts; unbind-before-kill rollback; exact-workspace UI warning/goals update; restart/no-inference and handoff replacement-order tests. Full cargo test green (159 lib, 421 bin; 3 ignored watcher tests), cargo build/release green. Live Tier 4 intentionally remains open until the paired arcmux info.device_id release is integrated; do not close this issue before real cmux/arcmux dispatch dogfood.

title: Render arcmux remote sessions as native Mission Control surfaces
description: Consume the released arcmux ref↔devbox remote-session and cmux surface-binding protocol so Mission Control can identify the exact remote agent behind a surface and render its state, goal, activity, and freshness with the same native list/detail semantics as local agents.
design: Use arcmux stable RemoteSessionLocator and explicit cmux surface bindings as identity authority. Read only safe local arcmux projections or loopback APIs; never infer remote identity from titles or terminal scraping. Preserve local workspace behavior and show disconnected remote state as stale rather than idle or missing.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A cmux surface explicitly bound to a remote arcmux locator resolves to the correct device/profile/session after Mission Control restart. 2. Workspace list and detail views visibly distinguish remote device and fresh/stale/gone state while using the same working/idle/waiting semantics as local agents. 3. Remote goal/history/artifact metadata appears only when allowlisted and available; missing private fields do not degrade or leak. 4. Mesh disconnect leaves the surface visible and stale; reconnect refreshes it without restarting Mission Control or retargeting. 5. Tests cover exact binding, multiple devices/profiles, stale/gone, unbound surfaces, malformed projections, and no local regressions. 6. Live ref↔devbox dogfood proves a real remote agent appears, changes state, survives disconnect/reconnect, and the released mc binary renders it.
notes: Shipped Mission Control commits d37ddf0 and 9d1f2ed to master. Arcmux contract merged in PR #6 at 56579d1 and released on ref/devbox. Full serial tests green (123 lib, 369 bin, all integrations; 3 existing watcher tests ignored), release build green. Live exact binding showed working→idle, fresh→stale→fresh on same locator during mesh-only disconnect, exact peek, exact yield, and gone cleanup.
close_reason: Released and live-validated exact native ref↔devbox surface visibility, recovery, peek, and yield.

title: Delay mission item relocation after checkbox toggle
description: When the user presses x on a mission or Mission History item, update the checkbox in place immediately. Keep the row in its current section for a 5-second settle window, then move completed items from Missions to Mission History or revived items back to Missions. A second toggle during the window must cancel/reverse the pending move so the list does not jump while the user is interacting.
acceptance_criteria: 1. x changes the checkbox immediately without moving the row. 2. After 5 seconds, completed active rows move to Mission History and revived history rows move to Missions. 3. Toggling again within 5 seconds cancels/reverses the pending relocation and restarts the settle timer. 4. Pending relocation survives ordinary redraws without duplicate rows or cursor jumps. 5. Tests cover both directions, reversal, focus/cursor stability, and app release.
notes: Fixed the live visual gap: trajectory_view now renders each Mission and expanded Mission History checkbox from Item.checked, so x is visible synchronously while the row stays in its original section until the dedicated five-second sweep. Added a render regression covering active [x] and revived history [ ]. Validation: targeted visual test, full serial suite (107 library + 336 binary + integration tests), git diff check, and cargo build --release all pass.
close_reason: Immediate checkbox rendering and five-second relocation released.

title: Design local-to-remote agent PR tracking
description: Design a Mission Control system that durably discovers and tracks every pull request generated during an agent conversation. Start with local agents and define a secure, incremental path for remote agents, including provenance, deduplication, status refresh, failure handling, UI integration, and rollout acceptance criteria.
design: Arcmux owns trace ancestry, generic artifact capture, durable bbolt outbox, shared ~/data/mux projections, and a hub-and-spoke Tailscale WebSocket with ref as the v1 hub. Mission Control owns GitHub reconciliation, provider cache, PR grouping/UI, and PR notification policy. Explicit PR-workflow emission is primary; safe hook extraction and turn-end provider reconciliation are safety nets. Remote peers persist and replay origin-sequenced events and bidirectional notification acknowledgements.
acceptance_criteria: A self-contained project-vault design specifies the local MVP, stable event/data contracts, remote transport and authentication path, UI behavior, failure modes, rollout phases, and objective acceptance criteria.
notes: Design written to /Users/blin/agents/obsProjects/mission-control/plans/arcmux-conversation-pr-mesh.md. Includes objective local, two-device, multi-device, restart, disconnect, security, privacy, deduplication, and notification acceptance criteria. Tailscale Serve/Grants assumptions validated against current official documentation; WebSocket upgrade through Serve remains an explicit Phase 0 spike.
close_reason: Completed self-contained local-to-remote arcmux PR tracking and notification mesh design, with rollout and acceptance criteria.

title: Fade detail cursor highlight when sidebar has focus
description: Make trajectory detail row highlighting reflect pane focus: active and cursor-following in Detail, visually faded or dismissed after returning to the workspace sidebar.

Applied to Mission, Mission history, section headers, surfaces, and Beads. Added Mission and Beads render regressions. Focused render tests, all trajectory-view tests, full serial suite, clippy, debug build, Release build, live l/h focus transition, and loaded-binary inode verification passed.
close_reason: Implemented, fully tested, and released with live focus-transition verification.

title: Redesign Mission lines as reversible checkbox workflow
description: Replace the flaky current/history positional editor with explicit one-line Mission items that can be completed and revived, preserve human-authored text, and remove abandoned empty insertions.
design: Persist active and completed missions as separate canonical Mission/Mission history sections. Normalize legacy positional rows on load. Add per-workspace transient history fold state; Enter toggles it. Mission x/X moves rows between sections, Mission dd is a no-op, and o creates a provisional human row removed on empty Esc. Regen preserves [h] rows/history and deterministically deduplicates similar agent rows.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Active Mission contains one-line checkbox-style items and supports multiple simultaneous missions. 2. X on an active mission completes it into folded Mission history; X on a revealed history item revives it into active Mission. 3. Mission history is folded by default and can be explicitly unfolded/folded without reordering unrelated rows. 4. o in active Mission inserts a new human mission; Esc removes it if it remains empty. 5. Human missions are marked [h], never model-edited, and regenerated agent missions are deduplicated against semantically similar human missions. 6. Existing task/Beads X and o behavior is unchanged. 7. Full tests, release build, and live cmux Mission workflow pass.
notes: Implemented explicit active/history Mission state, reversible x/X completion, Enter fold, Mission dd no-op, provisional o with empty-Esc cancellation, [h] preservation, deterministic agent deduplication, and completed-work non-revival. Verification: scoped rustfmt/diff checks, cargo clippy --all-targets (existing warnings only), cargo build, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1, cargo build --release, and isolated live cmux Release smoke all passed.
close_reason: Implemented, fully tested, and verified in an isolated live Release workflow.

title: Keep Mission non-empty from human or conversation intent
description: Mission regen can leave ## Mission empty. Preserve human-authored Mission text as the primary source; when no human Mission exists, synthesize one or more very short bullets from the workspace conversation summaries. Add regression coverage and validate live.
design: Post-LLM Mission reconciliation order: preserve non-empty saved Mission; otherwise accept non-empty generated Mission; repair empty generated Mission from latest user ask, then recent user explanation, then up to three session/surface summaries, then a short workspace fallback. Empty Mission is also a scheduler trigger even with zero pending events.
acceptance_criteria: Human-authored Mission survives regen as primary content; empty Mission falls back to concise conversation-derived bullets; generated Mission never remains empty when useful conversation context exists; full tests and release build pass.
notes: Validated with 5 new regression behaviors, full single-threaded suite, release build, clippy, CLI smokes, forced live regen of empty mc workspace, and automatic zero-event regen of empty obsidian workspace.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic non-empty Mission reconciliation and automatic empty-Mission regen scheduling. Saved human Mission remains authoritative; fallbacks are concise and capped. Full suite, release, and two live cmux paths passed.

title: Add locally selectable OpenAI short-text provider
description: Mission Control currently uses xAI for workspace prefixes, remote intent extraction, and per-surface overall summaries. Add an equivalent OpenAI Responses API provider selected by machine-local config, load its key from explicit config or the reflectionai GCP secret, configure ref for OpenAI, and surface configuration/secret failures as a non-fatal global TUI warning.
design: Add machine-local JSON config at ~/data/mission-control/config.json with short_text_provider (xai default, openai opt-in). Refactor the three short generations behind one concrete provider client; the selected provider is authoritative rather than silently falling through. Use OpenAI Responses API with gpt-5.4-mini and extract output_text from response output items. Resolve OpenAI credentials only when needed, with explicit flag/env precedence and bounded gcloud execution. Render sanitized credential/config failures in the global info layer. Configure ref locally for OpenAI.
acceptance_criteria:
1. All three xAI-backed short-text operations can run through the provider selected in ~/data/mission-control/config.json.
2. short_text_provider accepts xai or openai; missing config preserves xAI, and invalid config is surfaced without crashing.
3. On ref, local config selects openai; only the selected provider is called, with existing deterministic/no-result degradation on failure.
4. OPENAI_API_KEY/--openai-api-key wins; otherwise, when OpenAI is selected, mc runs gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=OPENAI_API_KEY_AGENTIC --project=reflectionai without persisting or logging the key.
5. A failed/empty/timed-out gcloud lookup does not prevent mc from starting and produces a persistent global warning in the TUI info layer.
6. Provider/config/API/secret/warning tests pass, the full single-threaded suite passes, live mc launches, and cargo build --release succeeds without warning-budget regression.
close_reason: Implemented and validated selectable OpenAI short-text provider, gcloud key lookup, and global warning

Added tests for j from last visible Mission history, k from next section, and G in Mission-only docs. title: Make Detail navigation stable for l and j/k
description: Boyan reports Detail is flaky: pressing l from Detail can jump directly into a surface, and j/k no longer consistently show highlighted trajectory cursor movement. Fix Detail key ownership so l does not switch/open surfaces from Detail and j/k reliably initialize/show the cursor highlight.
acceptance_criteria: Checklist: pressing l in trajectory-backed Detail does not switch to/open a cmux surface; l is either a no-op or an editor-owned key in Detail; j/k in trajectory-backed Detail initialize/preserve edit_state and produce a visible nav cursor highlight; j/k does not mutate detail_scroll; PageUp/PageDown and mouse wheel still scroll Detail; tests cover l routing and j/k visible cursor state; cargo test -- --test-threads=1, cargo build --release, git diff --check, and live cmux smoke pass.

Trajectory-backed Detail now initializes edit_state/cursor as soon as it is focused, and opening Detail resets detail_scroll to keep the cursor highlight on-screen. The trajectory router also owns l/Right when a trajectory is loaded. Verified focused tests, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1, cargo build, cargo build --release, git diff --check, and live cmux smoke: l from Detail stayed in Detail, j/k stayed in Detail without viewport scroll.
close_reason: Fixed Detail key ownership and cursor initialization: l/Right only open Detail from Sidebar and no-op in Detail, trajectory-backed Detail eagerly initializes the nav cursor and resets scroll on open, and l/Right are consumed by the trajectory router when loaded. title: Remove 60s hook_status staleness window
description: agent_state() only trusts hook_status if <60s old. State only changes on hook events, so absence of events = unchanged state. Make last hook verdict authoritative until next event.
close_reason: agent_state(): removed 60s hook_status freshness gate; last hook verdict authoritative until next event. Build clean, 230 tests pass.

title: Self-healing cmux event subscriber (respawn + reap orphans)

Also reaped orphan cmux-events subscribers (kill_on_drop + startup pkill).

title: mc fights blueprint histories layout: histories must live in ~/agents (Obsidian vault), not ~/data/Sessions
description:
TUI fails to load session data with: 'histories dir validation failed: ~/agents/histories points to .../Obsidian/Agents/Sessions, expected ~/data/Sessions'.

Root cause: mc hardcodes ~/data/Sessions as the canonical session-log store and even migrates the blueprint symlink away from the vault, contradicting the agents blueprint where ~/agents/histories -> obs/Agents/Sessions is canonical (541 real logs there vs 1 in ~/data/Sessions). Secondary bug: prompts::obsagents_root() and summarize::output_dir() fall back to a nonexistent ~/agents/Obsidian symlink instead of the real ~/agents/obsAgents.

Decision (Boyan): align mc to blueprint. Relax validate_histories_dir to dir+readable; stop setup.rs creating ~/data/Sessions and migrating the histories symlink; remove session_logs_dir; fix obsagents_root/output_dir fallbacks to ~/agents/obsAgents; update smoke tests. Release build + verify.
close_reason: Aligned mc to the agents blueprint. validate_histories_dir now just checks dir+readable (trusts the blueprint symlink); setup.rs no longer creates ~/data/Sessions or repoints ~/agents/histories (warns if missing); removed paths::session_logs_dir; fixed obsagents_root()/summarize::output_dir() fallbacks from nonexistent ~/agents/Obsidian to ~/agents/obsAgents. Updated 4 smoke tests (2 setup, 1 inverted migrate->preserve, 1 inverted backfill fail->accept). Verified: release backfill-window succeeds against the real vault-backed ~/agents/histories (5 workspaces/17 surfaces); setup leaves the blueprint symlink untouched. 224 bin + 11 smoke tests pass single-threaded (1 pre-existing parallel-race test unrelated).

title: Automate daily Obsidian Missions snapshots
description: Turn Mission Control's persisted workspace/surface state into a daily, device-scoped Obsidian Missions note so goals and current asks stay inspectable outside the TUI.
design: Mission Control window registries are authoritative. The projection reads every windows/*/window.json, admits only workspace IDs still present under active/, selects the newest record per workspace by updated_at, and sorts workspace/surface rows deterministically. It writes only between mission-control HTML markers using a same-directory temporary file plus atomic rename, preserves human text, and skips unchanged bytes. The reliable registry-write path invokes the projection best-effort so Obsidian failures cannot fail TUI refresh. `mc missions` invokes the same projector headlessly and never contacts cmux. F7 is addressed by consuming normalized per-surface registry intent instead of rejoining trajectories or session logs; F4 reachability is covered by the fake-cmux backfill E2E and the installed CLI.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every reliable Mission Control refresh updates ~/agents/obsAgents/Missions/sessions/<PT-date>-<device>.md from persisted window registries, and mc missions performs the same projection headlessly without contacting cmux. 2. Only workspace IDs still present under data/mission-control/active are emitted; duplicate/stale window records cannot create duplicate or cross-workspace rows. 3. Output is deterministic: workspace by name/id and surface by index/ref; each surface always includes title/ref/kind and includes overall goal/latest ask when present. 4. Repeated refreshes replace only the mission-control managed region, preserve all human-authored content outside it, and do not rewrite an unchanged file. 5. Missing device metadata, obsAgents, or usable current snapshot data fails non-destructively with an actionable error; automatic refresh logs the warning without failing the TUI refresh, while mc missions returns a nonzero exit. 6. Focused data and CLI tests prove creation, current-workspace filtering and ordering, replacement/preservation, idempotence, command reachability, and failure behavior. 7. Focused tests, single-threaded full suite, warning-budget build, release build, and a live generated note all pass.
notes:
Phase: VERIFY -> SPECIFY -> BUILD. Trigger: live cmux socket broken pipe. Existing 7 data tests and full suite passed before the interface addition. F4 requires an independently reachable entry point; F7 filtering remains unchanged.
BUILD: Added src/mc_data/missions.rs, `mc missions`, reliable-refresh hook, registry deserialization, README documentation, 7 data tests, 2 CLI tests, and a fake-cmux refresh assertion. Live `cmux ping` is unavailable in this shell with Broken pipe, so live TUI launch was not claimed; fake-cmux exercises the actual refresh pipeline. Existing running mc processes predate the release and need restart to load the automatic hook.
